title: Japan 12th in Global Innovation Ranking
paragraphs: Japan has ranked 12th in an annual report that lists countries on their innovation capabilities and results. Three other Asian countries — South Korea, Singapore and China — all made it into the top 10.

The Global Innovation Index (GII) is a ranking of 139 countries that is published each year by the World Intellectual Property Organization. It uses 79 indicators to measure how much a country has invested in innovation and how much innovation it produces.
Governments and business leaders around the world use GII data to make economic decisions, as well as understand how to encourage innovation.

The top three countries this year were Switzerland, Sweden and the US, with Switzerland ranking first for the 16th year in a row. Among Asian countries, South Korea ranked fourth, followed by Singapore in fifth, while China ranked 10th.

In 2025, Japan set itself a goal of reaching fourth or higher on the GII by 2035. Having moved up from 13th in the 2024 ranking, this is the second year in a row that Japan has reached 12th on the ranking.

The GII report said that Japan's industrial and corporate innovation was "among the strongest in the world." Japan also ranked first in the world for production and export complexity — a ranking based on a country's ability to produce a variety of complex products. And when it came to spending on research and development, Japan was third in the world.
The GII also ranks the world's top innovation clusters. These are areas within a country where there is a high number of inventors and scientific authors, as well as investment in innovation.
This year, China's Shenzhen-Hong Kong-Guangzhou cluster came first on this ranking. Japan's Tokyo-Yokohama cluster was second, while the Osaka-Kobe-Kyoto cluster was 10th.
